name: five_more_mistakes
summary: A fast-paced educational video essay analyzing YouTube editing rules with practical timeline demonstrations. The edit is characterized by seamless dialogue jump cuts, 8-bit retro title cards, and illustrative B-roll comparisons.

captions.notes: No continuous speech captions are used; text is reserved strictly for headlines, callouts, and technical labels.

headline.notes: Retro 8-bit monospace text inverted on solid black rectangular banners to introduce numbered sections.

callouts.notes: Monochrome pixel-styled annotation boxes with simple arrows point out edit points directly on NLE timeline captures.

transitions.notes: Tight audio-led jump cuts and J-cuts with subtle framing punch-ins between takes to conceal cut seams.

end_screen.tone: Casual and conversational sign-off inviting audience discussion.

rules: Cut conversational pauses aggressively, overlapping incoming speech slightly as J-cuts.
Alternate talking-head zoom levels between cuts to avoid static framing.
Introduce major topics using centered pixelated font over black title blocks.
Accompany technical explanations with real timeline UI capture and pointer arrows.
Stack side-by-side or vertical split-screen clips when demonstrating visual comparisons.
Curate dynamic music beds that shift genres to match topic mood changes.
Insert illustrative B-roll or movie clips within 3 seconds of mentioning a concept.
avoid: Dead air or unmotivated pauses between dialogue lines.
Full-screen burn-in captioning for all spoken words.
Flashy modern transition packs like hyper-zooms, light leaks, or glitch effects.
Unmotivated B-roll montages that lack narrative context.
